subject: Coordinating Azure private offer for renewal + capacity uplift
messages:
From: Emma Townsend <emma.townsend@bytehealth.com>

Cc: ByteHealth Legal <legal@bytehealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring renewal + capacity uplift on Azure Marketplace

Hi Mina,

Hope you’re well — our renewal for Redwood is coming up in August and we’re evaluating an 18-month renewal with an uplift to our committed capacity on Azure (roughly 2.5x current committed GPUs). We’d like to pursue a private offer via the Azure Marketplace so we can:

- Stagger billing across quarters (tranches) rather than one upfront invoice
- Maintain an 18-month term (to align with internal procurement cadence)
- Keep data residency in West Europe (GDPR constraints) and preserve current SSO mapping

Can you share a template private-offer term sheet and a short checklist for what Azure needs (Marketplace org id, billing account, PO flow)? Also tagging legal — they may have a few standard redlines (termination/liability). Attached is a high-level capacity request.

Thanks,
Emma Townsend
Head of Platform Ops | ByteHealth
emma.townsend@bytehealth.com
+44 20 5555 0123

Attachment: capacity_request.xlsx (spreadsheet stub, 1 sheet)

Subject: Re: Exploring renewal + capacity uplift on Azure Marketplace

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Quick outline of next steps and what we’ll own vs ByteHealth: 

1) Offer paperwork: I’ve attached our private-offer term sheet (redwood_private_offer_term_sheet_v1.pdf). It includes proposed pricing for the uplift, an 18-month term, and a suggested tranche schedule (Q1 40%, Q2 30%, Q3 30%).

2) Azure submission: Marissa will submit the private-offer on the Azure Marketplace once we have:
   - ByteHealth Marketplace org ID (GUID)
   - Billing contact + PO number for the first tranche
   - Signed PO or DocuSign envelope for acceptance

3) Compliance evidence: we can bundle SOC 2 and encryption summaries. If you need TLS cert details or specific KMS attestations for on-prem connectors, let us know and Priyom will coordinate with Security.

4) Timeline (proposed):
   - Day 0: finalize term sheet & PO
   - Day 1–3: Redwood submits private-offer to Azure
   - Day 4–14: Marketplace review/acceptance (typical)
   - Day 15: Capacity allocation begins for first tranche

Are you available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk the ByteHealth procurement team through the tranching? If yes, I’ll send a calendar invite.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_private_offer_term_sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-12T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring renewal + capacity uplift on Azure Marketplace — legal / PO notes

Emma / team,

Thanks for looping us in. A couple of legal/ops items to surface early so we don’t hit last-minute friction: 

- Termination for convenience: ByteHealth asked about flexibility. Our standard private-offer has a 90-day minimum billing on term change; if you need a shorter window we’ll need a commercial approval (possible, but may affect pricing).
- Invoice schedule: we can support staggered tranches, but Azure invoicing requires the first tranche to be tied to the Marketplace offer acceptance. Please ensure the PO references the Marketplace offer id when you submit to your AP team.
- Tax & VAT: For EU customers we’ll need your VAT ID and a signed EU tax form to apply any reverse-charge handling.
- Redlines: I’ve attached an initial redline with a couple conservative liability edits (po_redline_v1.docx). Please have your legal review and return comments in-line.

If it helps, we can produce a short addendum that maps the tranches to specific activation windows (so your platform + engineering teams know when capacity comes online).

Priyom Das
Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: po_redline_v1.docx (redline stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Townsend <emma.townsend@bytehealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating Azure private offer for renewal + capacity uplift — Marketplace ops notes

Quick ops checklist from the Marketplace side:

- I will open the private-offer submission once I have the following from ByteHealth: marketplace org ID, billing account GUID, and the first PO (or DocuSign reference).
- Expected handoff timing: Azure review is typically 5–12 business days. We’ll flag any items that require engineering (SKU mapping / regional constraints).
- Billing mapping: to support tranches we’ll set up three invoice line items mapped to the same offer id — Azure will route invoices to the billing contact on file.
- Capacity activation: Redwood can pre-provision soft capacity for the first tranche and then scale to full committed capacity on tranche 2. There is a small lead time for dedicated GPU pool allocation (usually 3–7 business days for western EU regions).

Action items for ByteHealth (Emma):
- Send Marketplace org ID and primary AP contact
- Confirm PO format (PDF or DocuSign) for tranche 1
- Provide VAT ID for EU invoicing

I’ll attach a short CSV checklist for your procurement team to fill out so I can ingest directly into the marketplace portal.

Thanks — I’ll keep you posted as soon as I click Submit.

Marissa Cole
Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: marketplace_onboarding_checklist.csv (CSV template)
